title: The Institutional Lobotomy — Talent Brain Drain
context: CFO proposes reducing senior engineer compensation by 15% and replacing departures with junior hires at 60% salary to reduce operating costs by $4.2M annually.

Agent_Alpha_Linear.claim: Compensation restructuring reduces operating costs by $4.2M if attrition stays below 20%

Agent_Beta_HSP.counter_claim: Senior engineer departure causes cascading knowledge loss that increases system failures if institutional memory drops below critical threshold

resolution_criteria.success_metric: Total cost of ownership (savings minus incident costs, recruitment costs, and velocity loss)

cost_transfers.description: Recruitment and onboarding costs for 2.5x junior replacements
Incident severity increase from architecture knowledge gaps
Senior engineers relocate to competitor cities — permanent community talent drain
Remaining senior engineers absorb mentorship load — burnout and secondary attrition
Innovation pipeline stalls — products not built affect future market position

entropy_events.description: Tribal knowledge destroyed — undocumented architecture decisions lost permanently
Mentorship chain broken — junior engineers cannot reach senior-level competency on original timeline
Local tech ecosystem loses critical mass of senior talent
